claim_verdicts.evidence: sql-explain, ANALYZE option: "Carry out the command and show actual run times and other statistics" (so plain EXPLAIN does not execute). using-explain 14.1.1: "The output of EXPLAIN has one line for each node in the plan tree ... Additional lines might appear, indented from the node's summary line, to show additional properties of the node." Lesson section 3 now matches.

using-explain 14.1.1: "Estimated start-up cost. This is the time expended before the output phase can begin ... Estimated total cost ... all available rows are retrieved ... Estimated number of rows output by this plan node ... Estimated average width of rows output by this plan node (in bytes)." sql-explain: "the start-up cost before the first row can be returned, and the total cost to return all the rows."

using-explain: "The costs are measured in arbitrary units determined by the planner's cost parameters"; "Note that the \"actual time\" values are in milliseconds of real time, whereas the cost estimates are expressed in arbitrary units; so they are unlikely to match up." Live: two runs of explain-analyze.sh gave identical costs, Execution Time 12.734 ms vs 6.307 ms for the same 1433.27-cost plan.

using-explain: "The very first line (the summary line for the topmost node) has the estimated total execution cost for the plan; it is this number that the planner seeks to minimize." sql-explain: "the planner makes an appropriate interpolation between the endpoint costs to estimate which plan is really the cheapest." (EXISTS/LIMIT use start-up cost; not relevant to the lesson's queries.)

using-explain: "The structure of a query plan is a tree of plan nodes"; "It's important to understand that the cost of an upper-level node includes the cost of all its child nodes." Captured join plan: children printed with '->' under their parent; HashAggregate 49.75 > Hash Join 44.55 > Index Scan 39.92.

sql-explain: ANALYZE "Carry out the command and show actual run times and other statistics". using-explain 14.1.2: "the loops value reports the total number of executions of the node, and the actual time and rows values shown are averages per-execution." Live run 2026-09-28: Planning Time and Execution Time lines printed after each EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan.

sql-explain: "Keep in mind that the statement is actually executed when the ANALYZE option is used. Although EXPLAIN will discard any output that a SELECT would return, other side effects of the statement will happen as usual. If you wish to use EXPLAIN ANALYZE on an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ... without letting the command affect your data, use this approach: BEGIN; EXPLAIN ANALYZE ...; ROLLBACK;" Live run: cancelled count 571 before and after.

planner-stats: "The query planner needs to estimate the number of rows retrieved by a query"; "Entries in pg_statistic are updated by the ANALYZE and VACUUM ANALYZE commands, and are always approximate even when freshly updated." Note: reltuples/relpages "are updated by VACUUM, ANALYZE, and a few DDL commands such as CREATE INDEX" — the lesson's "written by ANALYZE" is incomplete but not false.

routine-vacuuming 24.1.3: "The autovacuum daemon, if enabled, will automatically issue ANALYZE commands whenever the content of a table has changed sufficiently." 24.1.6: "Temporary tables cannot be accessed by autovacuum. Therefore, appropriate vacuum and analyze operations should be performed via session SQL commands."

using-explain (bitmap example): "Fetching rows separately is much more expensive than reading them sequentially, but because not all the pages of the table have to be visited, this is still cheaper than a sequential scan." Live, customer_id = 1 on donhang_perf: Seq Scan cost 3808.00; with enable_seqscan=off Bitmap Heap Scan 6416.92 (100.5 ms actual); with bitmap also off Index Scan 8879.39 (59.6 ms) vs Seq Scan 40.8 ms.

using-explain: "the child plan node visits an index to find the locations of rows matching the index condition, and then the upper plan node actually fetches those rows from the table itself." Glossary, Heap: "Contains the values of row attributes (i.e., the data) for a relation. The heap is realized within one or more file segments in the relation's main fork."
